``` r
library(gtropic)
```

`gtropic_data()` filters by place, by date and by storm. This vignette covers
each kind of filter and how they combine. The radius and window arguments,
which link rainfall and floods to storms, are covered in `vignette("linkage")`.

## How filters combine

Several values in one argument are combined with OR; different arguments are
combined with AND, as in `dplyr::filter()`:


``` r
# OR within an argument: every unit in the United States or Mexico
gtropic_data(WHO_ENTITY = c("United States", "Mexico"))

# AND across arguments: units named "San Jose" that are in Costa Rica
gtropic_data(ADM2_NAME = "San Jose", ADM2_GROUP = "CRI")

# AND across arguments: Hurricane Katrina's rows in the United States only
gtropic_data(STORM_NAME = "Katrina-2005", WHO_ENTITY = "United States")
```

When two filters exclude each other, the error names them:


``` r
gtropic_data(WHO_ENTITY = "Mexico", ADM2_GROUP = "USA")
#> Error in `resolve_scope()`:
#> ! No ADM2 units satisfy all of the geographic filters supplied.
#> ✖ Filters in play: `ADM2_GROUP` and `WHO_ENTITY`.
#> ℹ Values are combined with OR within an argument and AND across arguments, so
#>   these conditions must hold together.
#> ℹ Use `gtropic_adm2()` to explore valid combinations.
```

## Places

Five arguments select administrative units, and `polygon` selects them by
location.

| Argument | Matches | Case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ADM2_ID` | unit identifier | exact |
| `ADM2_NAME` | unit name | case-insensitive |
| `ADM2_GROUP` | country grouping code | case-insensitive |
| `WHO_ENTITY` | WHO entity, usually a country | case-insensitive |
| `WHO_REGION` | WHO region | case-insensitive |

Names are matched after trimming whitespace, and the results use the
dataset's own spelling. Every value must match: one misspelled country among
five stops the whole query, and the error suggests near matches.


``` r
gtropic_data(WHO_ENTITY = c("Untied States", "Mexcio"), date_range = 2005)
#> Error in `resolve_scope()`:
#> ! 2 values in `WHO_ENTITY` did not match any ADM2 unit.
#> ✖ "Untied States" - did you mean "United States"?
#> ✖ "Mexcio" - did you mean "Mexico"?
#> ℹ See `gtropic_adm2()` for the full list of valid values.
```

`gtropic_adm2()` lists the valid values:


``` r
gtropic_adm2()
#> # A tibble: 49,349 × 5
#>    ADM2_ID                 ADM2_NAME        ADM2_GROUP WHO_ENTITY  WHO_REGION
#>    <chr>                   <chr>            <chr>      <chr>       <chr>
#>  1 17698898B68993560499599 Ab Band          AFG        Afghanistan Eastern Medi…
#>  2 17698898B73770643817409 Ab Kamari        AFG        Afghanistan Eastern Medi…

#>  5 17698898B88187802806148 Ahmad Abad       AFG        Afghanistan Eastern Medi…
#>  6 17698898B56570025970807 Ajristan         AFG        Afghanistan Eastern Medi…

#>  9 17698898B86734293398191 Aliabad          AFG        Afghanistan Eastern Medi…
#> 10 17698898B28188212808936 Alingar          AFG        Afghanistan Eastern Medi…

```

### Filtering with a polygon

`polygon` takes an `sf` or `sfc` object and needs the optional `sf` package.
A unit is selected when its population-weighted centroid lies inside the
polygon:


``` r
library(sf)
#> Linking to GEOS 3.13.0, GDAL 3.8.5, PROJ 9.5.1; sf_use_s2() is TRUE

north_carolina <- st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)
nc_10to11 <- gtropic_data(
  polygon = north_carolina,
  date_range = c(2010, 2011),
  tables = c("wind", "adm2")
)
#> ℹ Polygon membership is year-dependent.
#>   Centroids were evaluated for 2 years (2010-2011); an ADM2 unit is included if
#>   its centroid fell inside the polygon in any of them.
#> Retrieving 0 files (0.0 B); 5 already cached.
nc_10to11$adm2
#> # A tibble: 98 × 5
#>    ADM2_ID                 ADM2_NAME ADM2_GROUP WHO_ENTITY    WHO_REGION
#>    <chr>                   <chr>     <chr>      <chr>         <chr>
#>  1 52423323B75735385248620 Alamance  USA        United States Americas
#>  2 52423323B44414006635896 Alexander USA        United States Americas
#>  3 52423323B93536446386656 Alleghany USA        United States Americas
#>  4 52423323B73600596363110 Anson     USA        United States Americas
#>  5 52423323B47317028722188 Ashe      USA        United States Americas
#>  6 52423323B91612624851462 Avery     USA        United States Americas
#>  7 52423323B44486980116087 Beaufort  USA        United States Americas
#>  8 52423323B7787272397887  Bertie    USA        United States Americas
#>  9 52423323B8015598177606  Bladen    USA        United States Americas
#> 10 52423323B12833551098527 Brunswick USA        United States Americas
#> # ℹ 88 more rows
```

Two points to keep in mind:

1. **The polygon needs a coordinate reference system.** A polygon in any CRS
   other than EPSG:4326 is transformed to match the published centroids;
   `reproject = FALSE` makes that an error instead.
2. **Membership can change between years.** Centroids move as populations
   shift, so a unit near the boundary can be inside in one year and outside in
   the next. A unit is selected if its centroid was inside in *any* year the
   query covers. A multi-year polygon query says so, and warns, listing the
   units, when membership actually varied. The full list is kept in the
   diagnostics; in North Carolina in 2010-2011 no unit changed, so it is
   empty:


``` r
gtropic_diagnostics(nc_10to11)$polygon_inconsistent
#> NULL
```

The named geographic filters do not change between years.

## Dates

`date_range` takes one or two endpoints; a single value is used for both, so
`2025` means all of 2025. `date_list` takes a vector of exact dates instead.
The two cannot be combined.

Partial dates expand to the start of their period for the first endpoint and
to the end for the second, so `c(2001, 2003)` covers three years:

| You write | Start becomes | End becomes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"2001"` or `2001` | `2001-01-01` | `2001-12-31` |
| `"2001-03"` | `2001-03-01` | `2001-03-31` |
| `"2001-03-04"` | as given | as given |
| a `Date` or `POSIXct` | as given | as given |

Dates that are not in ISO order are read in one order for all the values
supplied:


``` r
# "01/04/2001" alone could be 4 January or 1 April, but 19 cannot be a month,
# so both dates are read as month-day-year.
gtropic_storms(date_range = c("01/04/2001", "05/19/2001"))
#> # A tibble: 18 × 4
#>    STORM_ID      STORM_NAME    USA_ATCF_ID STORM_GENESIS_DATE_UTC
#>    <chr>         <chr>         <chr>       <date>
#>  1 2001018S12086 Charly-2001   SH062001    2001-01-17
#>  2 2001028S15128 Terri-2001    SH072001    2001-01-27
#>  3 2001039S11139 Winsome-2001  SH082001    2001-02-08
#>  4 2001039S13117 Vincent-2001  SH092001    2001-02-07
#>  5 2001047N09134 Unnamed-2001  WP012001    2001-02-16
#>  6 2001047S17157 Unnamed-2001  SH102001    2001-02-16
#>  7 2001049S17198 Oma-2001      SH112001    2001-02-18
#>  8 2001054S15155 Abigail-2001  SH122001    2001-02-23
#>  9 2001056S11163 Paula-2001    SH132001    2001-02-25
#> 10 2001060S19223 Rita-2001     SH142001    2001-02-28
#> 11 2001064S10052 Dera-2001     SH152001    2001-03-04
#> 12 2001091S11111 Walter-2001   SH172001    2001-04-01
#> 13 2001091S13094 Unnamed-2001  SH162001    2001-04-01

#> 16 2001106N04138 Unnamed-2001  WP022001    2001-04-16
#> 17 2001106S08137 Alistair-2001 SH202001    2001-04-15
#> 18 2001125N05129 Cimaron-2001  WP032001    2001-05-05
```

When more than one order fits, `ymd` is preferred, then `mdy`, then `dmy`, and
a warning names the choice:


``` r
gtropic_storms(date_range = c("01/04/2001", "05/06/2001"))
#> Warning: Dates "01/04/2001" and "05/06/2001" are ambiguous.
#> ℹ Interpreting as "mdy", so "01/04/2001" means "2001-01-04".
#> ℹ Rejected alternative: "dmy".
#> ℹ Set `date_format` to be explicit, e.g. `date_format = "dmy"`.
#> # A tibble: 18 × 4
#>    STORM_ID      STORM_NAME    USA_ATCF_ID STORM_GENESIS_DATE_UTC
#>    <chr>         <chr>         <chr>       <date>
#>  1 2001018S12086 Charly-2001   SH062001    2001-01-17
#>  2 2001028S15128 Terri-2001    SH072001    2001-01-27
#>  3 2001039S11139 Winsome-2001  SH082001    2001-02-08
#>  4 2001039S13117 Vincent-2001  SH092001    2001-02-07
#>  5 2001047N09134 Unnamed-2001  WP012001    2001-02-16
#>  6 2001047S17157 Unnamed-2001  SH102001    2001-02-16
#>  7 2001049S17198 Oma-2001      SH112001    2001-02-18
#>  8 2001054S15155 Abigail-2001  SH122001    2001-02-23
#>  9 2001056S11163 Paula-2001    SH132001    2001-02-25
#> 10 2001060S19223 Rita-2001     SH142001    2001-02-28
#> 11 2001064S10052 Dera-2001     SH152001    2001-03-04
#> 12 2001091S11111 Walter-2001   SH172001    2001-04-01
#> 13 2001091S13094 Unnamed-2001  SH162001    2001-04-01
#> 14 2001093S10062 Evariste-2001 SH182001    2001-04-02
#> 15 2001094S12172 Sose-2001     SH192001    2001-04-03
#> 16 2001106N04138 Unnamed-2001  WP022001    2001-04-16
#> 17 2001106S08137 Alistair-2001 SH202001    2001-04-15
#> 18 2001125N05129 Cimaron-2001  WP032001    2001-05-05
```

`date_format` fixes the order and silences the warning:


``` r
gtropic_storms(date_range = c("01/04/2001", "05/06/2001"), date_format = "dmy")
```

### Storms are selected by their genesis date

`date_range` and `date_list` select **storms whose `STORM_GENESIS_DATE_UTC`
falls in the period**: the UTC date of the storm's first best-track
observation, when it formed, not when it made landfall or reached a unit.
G-TROPIC's yearly storm, wind, zero-pair and track files are organised by the
same date, not by the published `SEASON`. Two consequences follow:

1. **Records can fall outside the period.** A storm that forms on
   30 September and lasts ten days contributes wind and rainfall into October,
   and a September query returns those rows too.
2. **A storm that formed before the period is left out**, even if it struck
   your region during it. A storm forming on 28 August that reaches Texas on
   3 September is not returned by:


``` r
gtropic_data(ADM2_GROUP = "USA", date_range = c("2002-09-01", "2002-09-30"))
```

### Selecting storms by when they reached a unit

Query a wider period, then filter `links` on `LOCAL_DATE_STORM_CLOSEST`, the
local date the storm passed closest to each unit:


``` r
library(dplyr)

# Two months either side catches storms that formed before September
res <- gtropic_data(ADM2_GROUP = "USA", date_range = c("2002-07-01", "2002-11-30"))

struck_in_september <- res$links |>
  filter(
    LOCAL_DATE_STORM_CLOSEST >= as.Date("2002-09-01"),
    LOCAL_DATE_STORM_CLOSEST <= as.Date("2002-09-30")
  )
```

Tropical cyclones rarely last more than two or three weeks, so two months
either side is generous.

## Storms

Three arguments select storms directly. `STORM_NAME` is matched
case-insensitively; `STORM_ID` and `USA_ATCF_ID` must match exactly.


``` r
gtropic_data(STORM_NAME = "Haiyan-2013")
gtropic_data(USA_ATCF_ID = "WP312013", date_range = 2013)
```

`STORM_ID` identifies one storm and is the key to use for queries, joins and
grouping. `STORM_NAME` is a convenience label: even a complete value such as
`"Haiyan-2013"` can match several storms, including in different basins, and
its year is the published `SEASON`, which need not be the genesis year. Look
the name up first, then use the `STORM_ID`:


``` r
gtropic_storms(STORM_NAME = "Haiyan-2013")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   STORM_ID      STORM_NAME  USA_ATCF_ID STORM_GENESIS_DATE_UTC
#>   <chr>         <chr>       <chr>       <date>
#> 1 2013306N07162 Haiyan-2013 WP312013    2013-11-02
```


``` r
haiyan <- gtropic_data(STORM_ID = "2013306N07162")
```

## Summary

- Values within an argument combine with OR; arguments combine with AND.
- Every filter value must match a published value.
- Dates select storms by genesis date, so returned records can extend beyond
  the period; use `LOCAL_DATE_STORM_CLOSEST` to select by impact date.
- Find storms by `STORM_NAME`, then query and join by `STORM_ID`.
